description: Three live nucleon-NF builders give three different Q_beta N=1 phases, spanning a SIGN CHANGE: single-wrap -0.05234, build_nucleon_nf (9 crossings, self-declared defective) -0.03541, build_atom_nf (gluon-complete, neutron-minus-hydrogen) +0.23558, all at convention C and the proton pin. The first two undershoot the required N=1 factor 0.99839767; the third overshoots by ~16x. They are three different SYSTEMS, not three bases, so this is not a convention ambiguity. The qou-pdix gate on branch 3 is therefore far worse than the 0.58% counit ratio the bean records.

checks.name: three_builders_give_three_distinct_alphas
checks.why: no two builders agree on the phase

checks.name: alpha_spans_a_sign_change
checks.why: the bare-nucleon builders give a NEGATIVE phase and the gluon-complete atom NF a POSITIVE one

checks.name: atom_nf_overcorrects
checks.why: the gluon-complete builder overshoots the required N=1 factor, the opposite side from the other two

checks.name: spread_far_exceeds_the_recorded_0p58pct
checks.why: the phase spread exceeds the magnitude of the smallest phase, so it is not the 0.58% the bean records from the COUNIT ratio

data.caveat: NOT like-for-like: build_atom_nf includes electrons (sigma_1^-1 per Z), so (0,1)-(1,0) is neutron minus HYDROGEN — the atomic-mass convention beta^- decay uses, arguably the physically right object, but a different object from the bare-nucleon difference the other two compute.
data.docstring_defect: pyhecke/atom.py:218 — build_atom_nf's docstring still carries 'No separate gluon dressing — B_3 IS the gluon structure', the exact sentence build_nucleon_nf retracts as unbacked while redirecting to build_atom_nf. There it is FALSE about its own function: lines 252-253 and 264-265 apply two gluon crossings per nucleon. Code is right, redirect is sound, only the line is stale.
